citations.assessment: The western transmission gives Rav Giddel’s interpretation of גדול as uttering the Explicit Name, and assigns “The great, mighty and awesome God” to Rav Mattana. An earlier report divides the attributions differently.
The checked account gives the instructions at the ritual immersion gate and the white-geese image.
The actors and direction of the complaint match the cited account; neither buyer eventually used the land.
The expanded Rabbi Abba bar Zavda heading names the colleagues and has its own dossier. Its pointer does not alter the land account.
The source specifically includes Rav Giddel in the list affected by Rav Huna’s long lectures.
The seating order is exactly Rabbi Zeira behind Rav Giddel, then Giddel before Rav Huna.
The checked folio has Rav Giddel reporting Zeiri on blood as an interposition. The named direction runs the other way in the Yerushalmi example.
Rabbi Zeira transmits from Giddul about a calf born on the festival. The direction remains as printed.

citations.assessment: The chain has Giddel, Rav Chiyya bar Yosef and Rav in the discussion of the covered structure.
The chain names Rav as the final authority, on betrothal with wheat.
The matching betrothal formulation has the chain end in Rabbi Yochanan here, whereas 7a gives Rav.
The cited page gives Giddel through Rav Chiyya bar Yosef from Rav about betrothal of a levirate widow. Its neighboring Rabbi Yochanan dialogue has a different attribution.
The checked witness assigns Rav to Kahana’s version and Shmuel to Tavyomi’s version, the reverse of Heilprin’s sequence. Both versions and the printed attribution remain visible.
This passage independently gives Rav Giddel in Rav’s name on a different subject.
The checked source names Yehoshua bar Abba, Giddel and Rav in the Torah reading teaching.
Two nearby reports give Giddel from Rabbi Yochanan.
This passage supplies Rav Kahana reporting Rav Giddel, who reports Rav.
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak gives both excluded patronyms and the stated practical reason. The preceding line also names Giddel of Naresh.
Giddel reports Rav in the discussion of a disciple before his teacher.
Giddel’s statement in Rav’s name is about swearing to fulfill a commandment.
The oath by Torah, Prophets and Writings is explicit in the discussion of partitions.
The vinegar discussion gives two versions of a Giddel report from Rav. The oath itself is explicit in the other folio.
The joined Rava bar Rav Huna, Rav Giddel and Rav chain recurs in two teachings.
The checked text has Rav, consistent with Heilprin’s proposed correction. The asserted older Rava reading requires additional print evidence.
This witness directly reads Rav Giddel in Shmuel’s name.
